verdict.rationale: Floot's own self-hosting doc says you can export the code and the database and deploy them anywhere, and other docs confirm the project is an exportable TypeScript/React app with a downloadable SQL dump. However, the evidence documents only the export step. It does not show how the exported app runs outside Floot, and the platform-brokered services (OAuth, email, scheduled jobs) are not shown to work off-platform. missing for 10: step-by-step deployment guidance for external hosts or own infrastructure, documentation of how Floot-managed services (brokered OAuth, email, push, scheduled jobs) behave when self-hosted, independent or hands-on corroboration of a successful self-hosted deployment.

support.subject: As a developer, I can deploy the generated app to an external host or my own infrastructure

citations.quote: you can export the code and the database and deploy them wherever you like.
A Floot project is a real TypeScript and React app — pages, components, and backend endpoints — and you can read or export all of it.
You can download a full SQL dump of your database at any time, on any plan
